draft.briefing: Hey, you're at Kollam Beach! It's also called Mahatma Gandhi Beach, and it was the first 'Beach Wedding Destination' in Kerala.
draft.hungryLine: Beach Road has a couple of places worth knowing, and one is famous for its mutton dishes.

moodReplies.show-me-around: Mahatma Gandhi Park is a 3 min walk, Kollam Port is about 16 min, and the Chinnakada Clock Tower is around 20 min away.
moodReplies.somewhere-to-chill: Mahatma Gandhi Park is just a 3 min walk, a calm green spot right by the beach.
moodReplies.surprise-me: Kollam Port goes back to AD 825, and Ibn Battuta counted it among the Indian ports he visited.

spots.name: Mahatma Gandhi Park
spots.detail: 3 min walk · Park by the beach, opened 1961

spots.name: Kollam Port
spots.detail: 16 min walk · One of India's oldest ports

spots.name: Chinnakada Clock Tower
spots.detail: 20 min walk · Travancore's first clock tower

legends.title: Karkidaka Vavubali
legends.body: Every Karkidakam month, thousands of people come to the beach to offer Bali to the souls of the departed. Men, women and children all take part.

tips.title: Don't swim here.
tips.body: Untreated sewage flows into the water, so enjoy the sand and leave the sea alone.

tips.title: Climb Thangassery Lighthouse in the afternoon.
tips.body: It's open 3-5PM, and the old fort ruins are a short shaded walk away.

story.title: An ancient port
story.body: Kollam Port was established, and from the ninth to the seventeenth centuries it was one of the coast's key ports.

story.title: Portuguese Kollam
story.body: The Portuguese set up what is now the Infant Jesus Cathedral in Thangassery.

story.title: Battle of Quilon
story.body: On 15 January 1809, Travancore troops under Velu Thampi Dalawa fought the East India Company for six hours.

story.title: A park by the sea
story.body: Vice President Zakir Husain opened Mahatma Gandhi Park on 1 January 1961.

story.title: Your turn
story.body: Kites, cashew and a very old port. Tell me which way you walked.
